Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 84, verses 16–25:

Explanation of the words:

*Bi-l-shafaq* (by the twilight): that is, by the redness in the horizon after the sun sets.

*Wa-ma waseq* (and what it gathers): that is, what it encompasses of creatures and others.

*Idha-ttasaq* (when it becomes full): that is, when it gathers and its light is complete, and that is on the bright nights.

*Tabaqan 'an tabaq* (stage after stage): that is, state after state: death, then life, then what follows of the states of the Resurrection.

*Fa-ma lahum la yu'minun* (then what is wrong with them that they do not believe): that is, what hinders them from believing in Allah and His Messenger and in meeting their Lord, though the proofs are many and are recited to them.

*Wa-idha quri'a 'alayhimu-l-Qur'an* (and when the Qur'an is recited to them): that is, it is recited to them and they hear it.

*La yasjudun* (they do not prostrate): that is, they do not humble themselves so as to believe and submit.

*Bima yu'un* (what they gather up): that is, what they collect in their records of disbelief and denial.

*Lahum ajrun ghayru mamnun* (for them is a reward not cut off): that is, not interrupted.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Fa-la uqsimu﴾ (So I swear), mean: the matter is not as you claim, that there is no resurrection and no recompense. He swears by the twilight, which is the redness of the horizon after the sun sets, and by the night and what it gathers, that is, what it gathers of every living creature, whether swimming in the water, flying in the sky, or roaming the earth, and by the moon when it becomes full, that is, when it gathers and its light is complete, and that is on the bright nights. The answer to the oath is the words of the Exalted, ﴿la-tarkabunna tabaqan 'an tabaq﴾ (you will certainly go through stage after stage), that is, state after state: death, then life, then the gathering, then the reckoning, then the recompense. These are states and terrors, so the matter is not as you imagine, that it is merely death and nothing more.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Fa-ma lahum la yu'minun wa-idha quri'a 'alayhimu-l-Qur'an la yasjudun﴾ (So what is wrong with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate), mean: what is wrong with people that they do not believe? What prevents them from believing in Allah and His Messenger and the Last Abode, despite the abundance of signs, the strength of the proofs, and the brightness of the evidence? Moreover, when the Qur'an is recited to them and they hear it, they do not submit, do not humble themselves, and do not fall down in prostration, despite what it carries of various kinds of proofs and evidences. The words of the Exalted, ﴿Bali alladhina kafaru﴾ (Rather, those who disbelieve), mean: instead of believing and submitting, they deny. ﴿Wa-Allahu a'lamu bima yu'un﴾ (And Allah is most knowing of what they gather), that is, what they hold in their hearts of disbelief and denial, and in their souls of envy, arrogance, rancor and hatred. Based on this, O Our Messenger, give them good tidings, that is, inform them of what will grieve them: a painful punishment, both swift and deferred. ﴿Illa alladhina amanu﴾ (Except those who believe): that is, those among them who believed in Allah, His Messenger, the signs of Allah, and His meeting, and did righteous deeds, performing the obligations and avoiding the prohibitions. ﴿Lahum ajrun﴾ (For them is a reward), that is, a reward with Allah until the day they meet Him, ﴿ghayru mamnun﴾ (not cut off), that is, not diminished or interrupted, in Paradise, the Abode of Peace. O Allah, make us among its people by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.
